episode_title: David Wachs built his company by writing handwritten notes.

real_qa.q: How did David Wachs come up with the idea for Handwritten?
real_qa.r: When leaving Sell It in 2012, Wachs wanted to send thank you notes to his clients and employees. He sat down to write them by hand but quickly found his hand cramped, he ran out of stationery, and faced other typical obstacles. This frustration made him think there had to be a better way to automate handwritten notes, which led him to start Handwritten the day after his earn-out was complete in 2014.

real_qa.q: What was Sell It before Handwritten?
real_qa.r: Sell It was a text messaging company David Wachs founded in 2004 and ran for 10 years. It started by providing property information through SMS when people texted numbers on real estate signs before Zillow existed. He quickly pivoted to serve multiple verticals including bars and restaurants with drink specials and coupons, and major retail clients like Abercrombie and Fitch and OfficeMax. For Abercrombie alone, the company was sending a million text messages per day. Wachs sold Sell It in 2012 to a marketing firm in Detroit.
real_qa.requete: Sell It text messaging company Abercrombie Fitch

real_qa.q: How many cards per day does Handwritten process?
real_qa.r: Handwritten tracks and processes 30,000 cards through an assembly line every day, ensuring the right card goes in the right envelope with the right type of stamp. This physical production requirement creates a significant moat for the business that protects it from being disrupted by AI software companies.

real_qa.q: Why did David Wachs stop offering prepaid business plans at Handwritten?
real_qa.r: Handwritten moved away from prepaid plans because they were based on the innovator's dilemma—the prepaid model was incredibly addictive revenue, offering $30,000 upfront instead of $30 monthly recurring, making it hard to abandon. However, Wachs decided to transition to an invoice model to better align the business, which took time to recoup the revenue bumps but ultimately created a healthier business model.
real_qa.requete: Handwritten prepaid plans invoice model pivot

real_qa.q: What employee transformation stories does Handwritten highlight?
real_qa.r: Wachs describes how Handwritten has transformed employee lives: a woman who previously cleaned toilets at a motel became head of quality assurance; another employee who initially needed physical paychecks to cash them was introduced to banking and eventually used her first credit card to buy a television; and a woman recovering from methane addiction was able to afford dental work and now has confidence to take photos with her grandchildren.

guest.bio_context: David Wachs is a serial entrepreneur from Phoenix, Arizona, who graduated from University of Pennsylvania's Wharton School. He founded Sell It in 2004, a text messaging company that he grew for 10 years and sold in 2012 to a marketing firm in Detroit, remaining as an employee for two years through the earn-out period. The day after his earn-out was complete in 2014, he launched Handwritten, which automates the sending of personalized handwritten note cards, a business he has now operated for 12 years.
